cases.note: the dead-man at start, cause start; a timer with nothing active changes nothing (§2.11)
the first arrival in the dead-man makes its provider active, cause sample, and is delivered (§2.9, §2.10)
a higher provider takes over at its first arrival, no hysteresis; a lower one's arrivals are counted not_active (§2.9)
the active misses its deadline once more than the deadline has passed: in time at its due instant, missed after it, cause deadline (§2.6, §2.9; timing.v1 §2.5)
an arrival exactly the deadline after the last is in time: no switch
missed, then back at its next arrival, cause sample: never withdrawn, it needs no re-admission
an event decides the time first: the active's arrival after its due instant makes two switches, its miss and its return
a miss decided at another provider's arrival: cause deadline, and the arrival delivered by the provider now active
every provider misses: the dead-man, cause deadline; then any arrival leaves it, cause sample (§2.11)
a withdrawal of the active: at once, cause withdrawn, a read again asked; its later samples are counted, never delivered, and re-admit nothing (§2.7)
re-admitted by its token heard declared, it is eligible again only at its next arrival, cause sample
re-admitted by a complete read showing a token held (core §8.1's read again)
a read not complete showing a token re-admits too: a read cannot invent a token
a read not complete showing none leaves the provider withdrawn
a withdrawal of a token never known held leaves none known held: withdrawn, failing toward a lower priority
a re-mint: the new token declared before the old one goes, nothing changes, no read asked (§2.7, core §8.1)
a re-mint whose new token the watch never heard: withdrawn, then re-admitted by the read again, and active at its next arrival
a withdrawal of a provider not active switches nothing, and asks a read again
a complete read replaces what was known held: the token it no longer shows is forgotten, and that token's withdrawal leaves the one it shows
a read not complete adds to what was known held: the first withdrawal leaves one, the second none
a read never makes a provider ineligible: a complete read showing no token of the active changes nothing (the deadline alone, as for a tokenless provider)
a move: the close's withdrawals and the reopen's telling are kept, then applied as one change when the round trip stands: nothing changes (§2.8)
a move: a withdrawal the reopen did not undo is applied when the round trip stands, cause withdrawn, a read again asked
a move: the reopen's telling then a withdrawal, kept in order, end withdrawn
a move: a read's result is kept as well, and a read showing a token held while the move is pending re-admits only when the round trip stands
a move: the deadline goes on meanwhile; a round trip standing with nothing kept changes nothing
a round trip standing with no move pending changes nothing
a provider withdrawn before a move, re-admitted by the reopen's telling when the round trip stands, active at its next arrival
the time first at a withdrawal: the active's miss (deadline), then the withdrawal of the provider it fell to (withdrawn)
identity: a key that is not concrete is discarded first (core R6), whatever else it would be
identity: keys that are not the role's stream's at any address are unresolved, never an arrival
identity: an address no entry matches is unbound, never a provider
identity: a templated stream, its parameter bound: the role's key at each address, another value unresolved
an expired sample (timing.v1) is no arrival: counted, never delivered, and the deadline runs from the last arrival
a delete sample is no arrival (timing.v1 §2.5): counted, never delivered, and it keeps no provider eligible
a governed provider's sample redundancy.v1 §2.10 does not accept is no arrival: it neither preempts nor keeps an address eligible
a wildcard entry: its addresses at its position, by byte order, autopilot above teleop (§2.4)
an address matched twice ranks at its first entry: safety inside lab/*, below autopilot
tokens of another interface, or at an address no entry matches, are no withdrawal and ask no read
a role bound to nothing holds the dead-man for good (§2.2, §2.11)
the walkthrough: twist_cmd.v1, deadline 100 ms, safety silent then back

description: arbitration.v1 §2.5 to §2.11: one consumer's arbitrated role, and the events its runtime hands it in order -> after each event, what it decides. The role: interface (the required interface's id), resource (the stream's kind token and template), params (its parameter bindings, resolved), deadline_ms, and bindings (the entries in their configured order, as rankings.json reads them). Each event has at, an instant in ms on the consumer's monotonic clock, never decreasing, and event: "start" (first, once); "sample" with key (base-relative), and delete: true (a delete sample), expired: true (timing.v1 reads it expired) or incumbent: false (the required interface is governed and redundancy.v1 §2.10 does not accept it), each absent otherwise; "declared" or "withdrawn" with token, an interface token's key zk2/<system>/<service>/@zk/alive/<iface>/<instance>/<fp16> the watch heard (one of another interface, or at an address no entry matches, is ignored); "read" with address, complete and held (the instance ids holding the required interface's token there, as the read shows them); "moved" (the watch session's transport closed or opened); "stood" (the round trip asked after the last move stands); "tick" (the timer fired). The rules: a provider is eligible at t when it is not withdrawn and its last arrival a (since its last re-admission) has t <= a + deadline_ms (timing.v1 §2.5: missed once more than the deadline has passed). Each event at t first decides the time: an active provider not eligible at t is left for the eligible provider of highest rank at t, or none, cause deadline. Then the event: a sample's outcome is the first of wild (its key holds *), unresolved (not zk2/<system>/<service>/<interface>/<token>/<chunks> with the chunks matching the template and every parameter's chunk equal to params' value), unbound (no entry matches the address), deleted, expired, not_incumbent; otherwise it is an arrival, which sets the provider's last arrival unless it is withdrawn, and its outcome is delivered when its provider is active after the event, else not_active. A declaration adds its instance to those known held at its address and re-admits it (withdrawn ends; its arrivals stay forgotten). A withdrawal removes its instance; when none is then known held, the provider is withdrawn, its last arrival forgotten, and a read again asked (reread). A read: complete replaces the instances known held there, not complete adds to them; any then known held re-admits it; a read never withdraws. From a moved until a stood, declarations, withdrawals and reads are kept and change nothing; at that stood they are applied in order to the instances known held, as one change: an address left with none known held, a withdrawal of it among them, ends withdrawn (arrivals forgotten, reread); one withdrawn before them and left with one known held ends re-admitted; any other is unchanged. A stood with nothing pending changes nothing. After the event the active provider is the eligible provider of highest rank, or none: a change is a switch, cause sample when the event is an arrival of the provider now active, else withdrawn. "start" makes one switch, from null to null, cause start: the dead-man. expect[i] is, after event i: switches (each {from, to, cause}, null meaning none, the dead-man; at most a deadline one then the event's own), active (an address or null), due (the active provider's last arrival + deadline_ms, or null), outcome (for a sample), and reread (the addresses to read again, in rank order, when any).
